aevo-ausbildung_planen-01.question: Your management is considering stopping in-house training and instead only hiring fully qualified skilled workers on the labour market. You have been asked to make the case for in-house training at the next leadership meeting. Which line of argument best matches the competence goal of Handlungsfeld 1?

options.a: Training is above all a statutory duty of the company that nobody can avoid
options.b: Training is always the cheapest form of recruitment, because apprentices cost less than skilled workers
options.c: Set benefit against cost: securing the pipeline of skilled workers, qualification tailored to your own work and business processes, retention and employer attractiveness - and put the cost of training openly alongside that
options.d: Point to the reputational gain and deliberately leave the cost question open, because it cannot be answered seriously

aevo-ausbildung_planen-01.explanation: § 3(1) no. 1 AEVO requires the ability to "present and justify" the advantages and benefits of in-company training - a reasoned trade-off, not a marketing message. The Rahmenplan makes this explicit in HF 1.1 with "highlighting the benefit of training while also taking the cost to the company into account", and lists as example content: securing skilled-worker supply against demographic change, social responsibility, competitive advantage, flexibility, innovative capacity, and direct and indirect benefit. Answer (a) is wrong: there is no general duty to train in the BBiG - the BBiG regulates the conditions under which training is permitted (§§ 27-30 BBiG), not that a company must train. (b) asserts a cost claim that cannot be sustained in such blanket form. (d) misses exactly the cost analysis the Rahmenplan demands.

aevo-ausbildung_planen-02.question: A colleague who has twice been formally censured by the competent chamber for serious breaches of the Vocational Training Act is to take on new apprentices. How do you assess this?

options.a: Unproblematic, as long as she is professionally qualified and can prove her technical expertise
options.b: She is not personally suitable - repeated or serious breaches of the BBiG rule out personal suitability, and without personal suitability nobody may take on apprentices
options.c: Unproblematic, because personal suitability is only required for training, not for taking on apprentices
options.d: She may take them on, but must additionally appoint a second trainer

aevo-ausbildung_planen-02.explanation: § 29 BBiG names two standard examples of missing personal suitability: someone who is barred from employing children and young people, and someone who has repeatedly or seriously breached the BBiG or the rules issued under it. § 28(1) sentence 1 BBiG makes it explicit: only a person who is personally suitable may take on apprentices - so personal suitability is required precisely for taking apprentices on, not only for training them (sentence 2 additionally requires professional suitability for actually training). That makes (c) wrong. Professional suitability cannot compensate for missing personal suitability, so (a) and (d) miss the point. Supervision rests with the competent chamber under § 76(1) BBiG.

aevo-ausbildung_planen-03.question: A company wants to appoint a long-serving, technically very experienced employee as the responsible trainer, although he has no relevant final examination, no degree, and no formally recognised equivalence. What applies under § 30 BBiG?

options.a: Ten years of work experience automatically replaces the qualification
options.b: It is enough that he passes the AEVO examination - his occupational qualification is irrelevant for that
options.c: He may train if the apprentices additionally attend a vocational school
options.d: Only a person holding both the occupational and the vocational/work-pedagogical skills is professionally suitable; the occupational part requires one of the qualifications listed in § 30(2) BBiG plus an appropriate period of practice - lacking both, he can only assist under a trainer's responsibility per § 28(3) BBiG

aevo-ausbildung_planen-03.explanation: § 30(1) BBiG defines professional suitability in two parts: occupational AND vocational/work-pedagogical skills, knowledge and abilities. The AEVO examination covers only the second half - which makes (b) wrong. The occupational half requires, under § 30(2) BBiG, one of the five proofs listed there (a relevant final examination; the § 1(6) BBiG assessment procedure with full comparability; a recognised examination or school final examination; a degree; or a foreign qualification formally recognised as equivalent) AND an appropriate period of practical work in the occupation. Work experience alone is not an independent route - so (a) is wrong. Absent those conditions, § 28(3) BBiG remains: a person who, deviating from § 30 BBiG, has the necessary occupational skills and is personally suitable may assist - under a trainer's responsibility, but not as the responsible trainer.

aevo-ausbildung_planen-04.question: You are checking whether your 9-person company is suitable for a training occupation and find that three positions of the training framework plan cannot be delivered, because you lack the relevant machinery. What follows from that?

options.a: The training establishment still counts as suitable if the missing content is delivered through measures outside the establishment - e.g. in a training consortium or at an inter-company training centre
options.b: The establishment is unsuitable; the occupation cannot be trained in this company
options.c: The missing content may be made up in vocational-school lessons; the school is responsible for that
options.d: The training period must be extended by the missing share

aevo-ausbildung_planen-04.explanation: § 27(2) BBiG governs exactly this case: "An establishment in which the required occupational skills, knowledge and abilities cannot be delivered in full counts as suitable if these are delivered through training measures outside the establishment." § 3(1) no. 5 AEVO mirrors this in the competence profile and expressly names consortium training, inter-company and external training; § 10(5) BBiG provides the legal form of consortium training. (b) is therefore too strict. (c) confuses the learning venues: under § 2(1) no. 2 BBiG the vocational school delivers the school-based part and does not substitute for company training-framework positions. (d) confuses a suitability gap with the extension grounds in § 8(2) BBiG, which attach to the individual apprentice's training goal, not to the company's equipment.

aevo-ausbildung_planen-05.question: The owner of a retail business holds a business-administration degree but has no final examination in the occupation she wants to train in, and does not intend to deliver the training herself. May her company take on apprentices?

options.a: No - without the owner's professional suitability the company is excluded
options.b: Yes, with no further conditions; professional suitability is only examined for sole traders
options.c: Yes - she must then appoint personally and professionally suitable trainers who deliver the training content directly, responsibly and to a substantial extent
options.d: Yes, if she contracts an external training provider to deliver the entire training

aevo-ausbildung_planen-05.explanation: § 28(1) BBiG separates two roles: taking on apprentices requires only personal suitability, training them requires personal and professional suitability. § 28(2) sentence 1 BBiG follows on: a person who is not professionally suitable, or who does not train personally, may only take on apprentices if they appoint personally and professionally suitable trainers "who deliver the training content in the establishment directly, responsibly and to a substantial extent". This is the standard arrangement in medium and large companies - the company is the Ausbildender, and the expressly commissioned person is the Ausbilder. So (a) is too strict and (b) is wrong. (d) misses the criterion "in the establishment, directly and to a substantial extent": training may not be outsourced entirely. In addition, § 28(2) sentence 2 BBiG permits digital mobile training to an appropriate extent.

aevo-ausbildung_planen-06.question: A company with two skilled workers wants to take on six apprentices next year. Which additional check does § 27 BBiG require, beyond the company's equipment?

options.a: Whether enough vocational-school places are free in the district
options.b: Whether the number of apprentices is in an appropriate ratio to the number of training places or to the number of skilled workers employed - otherwise suitability is lacking, unless training is nonetheless not put at risk
options.c: Whether the works council has approved the hires
options.d: Whether the training allowance at least matches the collectively agreed pay

aevo-ausbildung_planen-06.explanation: § 27(1) BBiG names two cumulative suitability requirements for the establishment: no. 1 suitability by nature and equipment, no. 2 an appropriate ratio between the number of apprentices and the number of training places or skilled workers employed - with the express escape clause "unless training would nonetheless not be put at risk". This is the classic trainer-to-skilled-worker ratio the competent chamber examines as part of its § 76(1) BBiG supervision. Vocational-school places (a) are not a suitability requirement for the establishment. Works-council involvement (c) follows from § 99 BetrVG and §§ 96-98 BetrVG, not from § 27 BBiG. Pay appropriateness (d) is governed by § 17 BBiG, again not by § 27.

aevo-ausbildung_planen-07.question: Your technical line manager wants to draw up the company training plan "entirely freely to suit our needs" and to drop individual positions of the training framework plan that the company does not need. How do you react as the trainer?

options.a: Agree - the training framework plan is a recommendation of the BIBB main committee
options.b: Agree, as long as the competent chamber raises no objection
options.c: Refuse, because the works council must adopt the plan first
options.d: Refuse: for a recognised training occupation, training may only follow the training regulation; the training framework plan is part of that regulation and therefore a binding minimum - the freedom lies in how content is sequenced and timed, not in leaving content out

aevo-ausbildung_planen-07.explanation: § 4(3) BBiG is unambiguous: "For a recognised training occupation, training may only follow the training regulation." Under § 5(1) BBiG the training regulation lays down, among other things, the occupational profile (no. 3) and the training framework plan as guidance on the substantive and temporal structure (no. 4) - both are statutory instrument law, not recommendation. That makes (a) wrong: BIBB main-committee recommendations (such as the AEVO Rahmenplan itself) are recommendations, training regulations are statutory instruments. (b) makes the legal position depend on an objection that is not needed. (c) confuses competences: the works council has participation and co-determination rights in vocational training under §§ 96-98 BetrVG, but does not adopt a company training plan. What can be freely designed, per § 3(2) no. 1 AEVO, is the translation into occupation-typical work and business processes.

aevo-ausbildung_planen-08.question: Your company wants to deliver part of the training as "digital mobile training" - trainer and apprentice are not in the same place at the same time. Which conditions does § 28(2) sentence 2 BBiG set for this? (3 correct answers)

options.a: Information technology is used for the delivery
options.b: The share of digital mobile training may not exceed 25 percent of the training time
options.c: The training content and the respective locations are suitable for remote delivery
options.d: The competent chamber must give prior written consent to digital mobile training
options.e: The quality of delivery is equivalent to that of being in the same place at the same time

aevo-ausbildung_planen-08.explanation: § 28(2) sentence 2 BBiG sets out exactly three conditions (nos. 1-3): the use of information technology; the suitability of the training content and of the respective locations for remote delivery; and equivalence of delivery quality. No. 3 is fleshed out by a statutory example: equivalence exists in particular where the trainer is reachable at any time during normal business hours, steers and accompanies the learning process, and checks learning progress. The extent is limited only qualitatively - "to an appropriate extent" in the opening clause; the Act contains no fixed percentage cap as in (b). Prior consent from the competent chamber (d) is also not required; § 28(2) sentence 3 BBiG merely empowers the BIBB main committee to issue recommendations on the design. Note on exam mechanics: for closed-form tasks with more than one correct option, the AEVO exam applies the all-or-nothing principle - every correct option must be marked.

aevo-ausbildung_planen-09.question: In your workshop, experienced journeymen are to supervise individual training phases. You remain the responsible trainer. Which requirements apply to these assisting skilled workers?

options.a: They must have passed the AEVO examination themselves, because they deliver training content
options.b: They do not need the specific requirements of § 30 BBiG, but must have the occupational skills, knowledge and abilities necessary for the delivery and be personally suitable - and they work under your responsibility
options.c: They must be registered as trainers with the competent chamber
options.d: They may only observe and must not deliver any training content

aevo-ausbildung_planen-09.explanation: § 28(3) BBiG creates a distinct, lower threshold for exactly this role: "Under the responsibility of the trainer, a person who is not themselves a trainer but who, deviating from the specific requirements of § 30, has the occupational skills, knowledge and abilities necessary to deliver training content and is personally suitable, may assist in vocational training." The AEVO's vocational/work-pedagogical suitability is therefore not required of them - (a) is wrong, and a blanket ban as in (d) even less so. What must be registered under §§ 34 f. BBiG is the training relationship, not the assisting skilled worker - so (c) is wrong. The flip side of the lower threshold is your responsibility: § 3(1) no. 7 AEVO expressly requires coordinating the tasks of those assisting in training "taking account of their functions and qualifications" - i.e. brief them, delimit their tasks clearly, and check the results.

aevo-ausbildung_planen-10.question: A new colleague asks you where in the rulebook she can find the binding training duration and the guidance on how training content is structured and sequenced. What do you answer?

options.a: In the training contract - both are laid down there for the first time
options.b: In the vocational school's framework curriculum adopted by the standing conference of education ministers
options.c: In the training regulation: § 5(1) BBiG requires it to lay down, among other things, the training duration (no. 2, as a rule two to three years) and the training framework plan as guidance on the substantive and temporal structure (no. 4)
options.d: In the competent chamber's examination regulation

aevo-ausbildung_planen-10.explanation: § 5(1) BBiG lists five mandatory contents of every training regulation: the occupational title (no. 1), the training duration - as a rule not more than three and not less than two years (no. 2) -, the occupational profile (no. 3), the training framework plan as guidance on substantive and temporal structure (no. 4), and the examination requirements (no. 5). The training contract (a) carries these details over under § 11(1) sentence 2 nos. 2 and 3 BBiG, but does not originally establish them. The school framework curriculum (b) is the training regulation's counterpart at the vocational-school venue and does not govern company-side structuring. The examination regulation (d) governs admission, the structure of the examination, assessment standards and resits under § 47(2) BBiG - not the training content.

aevo-ausbildung_planen-11.question: A young woman applies for a training place. She does not yet meet the occupation's requirements but shows clear interest and development potential. Which option belongs to Handlungsfeld 1's "measures preparing for vocational training"?

options.a: Immediately concluding a training contract with an extended six-month probationary period
options.b: An unpaid twelve-month company internship as a substitute for the first year of training
options.c: A training contract with a shortened training duration from the outset
options.d: A pre-vocational measure such as an entry-level qualification (Einstiegsqualifizierung) or assisted training, coordinated with partners like the employment agency, youth careers agency, or a training provider

aevo-ausbildung_planen-11.explanation: § 3(1) no. 6 AEVO requires assessing the scope for using measures that prepare people for vocational training. The 2023 Rahmenplan expressly names, in HF 1.6, entry-level qualification and assisted training as example content, and schools, the employment agency, youth careers agencies and training providers as cooperation partners. Legally, pre-vocational preparation is a distinct instrument: § 1(2) BBiG describes it as delivering the foundations for acquiring occupational competence in order to lead into vocational training. (a) is unlawful: § 20 BBiG caps the probationary period at four months. (b) is unlawful, because a training relationship carries a duty to pay (§ 17(1) BBiG) and § 25 BBiG voids agreements that deviate to the apprentice's disadvantage. (c) inverts the point of shortening: § 8(1) BBiG presupposes an expectation that the training goal will be reached in the shortened time.

aevo-ausbildung_planen-12.question: An adviser from the competent chamber announces a visit to your training establishment and asks in advance for documents on how training is progressing. Your management asks whether this is permissible. What do you answer?

options.a: No - the chamber may only act on a specific complaint
options.b: Yes: the chamber supervises the delivery of vocational training and promotes it through advice; on request, those providing training must give the necessary information, produce documents, and permit inspection of the establishment
options.c: Yes, but only with the works council's prior consent
options.d: No - supervision rests exclusively with the supervisory authority under the Youth Employment Protection Act

aevo-ausbildung_planen-12.explanation: § 76(1) BBiG gives the competent chamber a twofold mandate: it supervises the delivery of pre-vocational preparation, vocational training and retraining AND promotes them through advice, appointing advisers for that purpose. § 76(2) BBiG spells out the duty to cooperate: give information, produce documents, permit inspection - each on request and without needing a triggering incident, which is why (a) is wrong. There is no works-council consent requirement (c). (d) is incomplete: supervision under the JArbSchG exists alongside, and § 76(5) BBiG even obliges the chamber to report relevant observations to that authority. As a limit on the duty to inform, § 76(4) BBiG provides a right to refuse answers that would risk self-incrimination.

aevo-ausbildung_vorbereiten-01.question: You are drawing up a company training plan for the first time. How do you proceed methodically so that the plan matches both the training regulation and your real workflows?

options.a: Work through the training framework plan position by position, in the same order as it appears in the regulation
options.b: First list the existing departments and place apprentices wherever capacity happens to be free
options.c: Map the training framework plan's positions onto the company's occupation-typical work and business processes, derive a rotation/deployment plan with substantive and temporal structure from that, and check feasibility with the assisting skilled workers
options.d: Adopt the vocational school's framework curriculum so that company and school proceed identically

aevo-ausbildung_vorbereiten-01.explanation: § 3(2) no. 1 AEVO words the competence precisely: on the basis of a training regulation, draw up a company training plan "oriented in particular to occupation-typical work and business processes". The 2023 Rahmenplan fleshes this out in HF 2.1 with the "relationship between the substantive and temporal structure in the training framework plan and the company's work and business processes", with rotation plans, consideration of individual learning prerequisites, and expressly with "checking the feasibility of training with the assisting skilled workers". (a) confuses guidance with a prescribed order - under § 5(1) no. 4 BBiG the training framework plan is guidance on structuring, not a checklist to be worked through. (b) inverts the logic: capacity would then drive training rather than the reverse. (d) confuses the learning venues - the school framework curriculum is not the company plan; aligning the two is learning-venue cooperation under § 2(2) BBiG.

aevo-ausbildung_vorbereiten-02.question: A training contract is agreed orally on 5 June; training starts on 1 August. By when, and in what form, must the essential contract content be recorded?

options.a: An oral agreement suffices; text form is only needed for minors
options.b: Without undue delay after conclusion of the contract, and at the latest before training starts, in text form
options.c: Within four weeks after training starts, in written form with an original signature
options.d: By the end of the probationary period, in text form

aevo-ausbildung_vorbereiten-02.explanation: § 11(1) sentence 1 BBiG: those providing training must record the essential content of the contract in text form "without undue delay after conclusion of the training contract, and at the latest before training begins". Two deadlines apply together - without undue delay AND at the latest before the start. Text form (§ 126b BGB) suffices; the Act does not require a handwritten signature for the record, so (c) is wrong on both form and deadline. Where the record is electronic, § 11(2) sentence 2 BBiG requires it to be transmitted so recipients can save and print it, and receipt must be evidenced. The training contract itself is valid without any particular form - which is why (a) is nevertheless wrong in result: the duty to record exists regardless of age. (d) confuses the recording deadline with the probationary period. Note also the retention period: the record and the receipt evidence must be kept for three years after the end of the year in which the relationship ended (§ 11(2) sentence 4 BBiG).

aevo-ausbildung_vorbereiten-03.question: Which details must the record of the training contract contain under § 11(1) sentence 2 BBiG? (4 correct answers)

options.a: Duration of the probationary period
options.b: Duration of the regular daily training time
options.c: The names of the appointed trainers
options.d: The conditions under which the training contract may be terminated
options.e: The form of the training record (Ausbildungsnachweis)

aevo-ausbildung_vorbereiten-03.explanation: § 11(1) sentence 2 BBiG lists twelve minimum details. They include no. 5 duration of the regular daily training time, no. 6 duration of the probationary period, no. 10 the conditions under which termination is possible, and no. 12 the form of the training record under § 13 sentence 2 no. 7 BBiG. The list further requires the parties' names and addresses (for minors also those of their legal representatives), the nature, substantive and temporal structure and goal of the training, start and duration, the establishment and any measures outside it, payment and amount of the allowance including its composition, payment or compensation for overtime, the length of holiday, and a general reference to applicable collective and works agreements. The names of the appointed trainers (c) are NOT on this list - the appointment itself follows from § 28(2) BBiG but is not a mandatory content of the contract record. Under § 11(3) BBiG the same rules apply to contract amendments.

aevo-ausbildung_vorbereiten-04.question: Your HR department presents a draft training contract. Which of the following clauses are void under § 12 BBiG? (3 correct answers)

options.a: An undertaking, given during the last six months of the training relationship, to enter an employment relationship after it ends
options.b: A contractual penalty of EUR 500 for unexcused absence
options.c: An obligation on the apprentice to reimburse the cost of training if they drop out
options.d: An agreement on a three-month probationary period
options.e: A clause capping the apprentice's damages claims at EUR 1,000

aevo-ausbildung_vorbereiten-04.explanation: § 12(2) BBiG declares four types of agreement void: no. 1 an obligation on the apprentice to pay compensation for the training (which catches the cost-reimbursement clause), no. 2 contractual penalties, no. 3 the exclusion or limitation of damages claims, and no. 4 fixing damages at flat rates. § 12(1) BBiG additionally voids post-contractual restraints of trade - but makes exactly one exception: an undertaking entered into during the last six months of the training relationship to enter an employment relationship with the training provider afterwards is permitted. So (a) is valid. A three-month probationary period (d) falls within the range of § 20 BBiG (at least one, at most four months) and is likewise valid. Alongside this, § 25 BBiG voids any agreement that deviates from this part of the Act to the apprentice's disadvantage.

aevo-ausbildung_vorbereiten-05.question: A line manager wants to agree a six-month probationary period for a retrainee, "so we can really see whether he fits". How do you assess that for a vocational training relationship?

options.a: Permissible if both sides expressly agree it in writing
options.b: Permissible if the competent chamber approves it
options.c: Not permissible: the training relationship begins with the probationary period, and it must be at least one month and at most four months
options.d: Permissible, because the probationary period in a training relationship can be freely agreed

aevo-ausbildung_vorbereiten-05.explanation: § 20 BBiG consists of two short sentences: "The vocational training relationship begins with the probationary period. It must be at least one month and may be at most four months." The range is mandatory - under § 25 BBiG any agreement deviating from this part of the Act to the apprentice's disadvantage is void, and a six-month probation operates to their disadvantage, because during probation either side may terminate at any time without notice under § 22(1) BBiG. Neither an agreement between the parties (a) nor chamber approval (b) can widen the range; (d) is simply wrong. The length of probation must also appear in the contract record under § 11(1) sentence 2 no. 6 BBiG. For comparison: under § 26 BBiG the statutory probationary period may be shortened for other contractual relationships (e.g. internships) - but not extended.

aevo-ausbildung_vorbereiten-06.question: The training contract is signed. Your administrator intends to apply for registration with the competent chamber "sometime before training starts". What applies?

options.a: Registration is voluntary and only serves statistical purposes
options.b: The application must be made without undue delay after the training contract is concluded, in writing or electronically, with a copy of the contract record and the receipt evidence
options.c: The application must be made within three months after training starts
options.d: The apprentice applies for registration themselves at the vocational school

aevo-ausbildung_vorbereiten-06.explanation: § 36(1) sentence 1 BBiG obliges the training provider to apply for "registration in the register without undue delay after the training contract is concluded"; sentence 2 allows a written or electronic application and requires a copy of the contract record and the receipt evidence. Sentence 3 permits reference to a company training plan already held by the chamber; sentence 4 extends the duty to changes in the essential contract content. Registration is not a formality: under § 43(1) no. 3 BBiG it is a precondition for admission to the final examination, which is why (a) is wrong - a missing registration can ultimately bar the apprentice from the examination (the provision only exempts cases for which neither the apprentice nor their legal representatives are responsible). § 3(2) no. 5 AEVO names exactly this task in the competence profile. (c) and (d) put the deadline and the responsibility in the wrong place.

aevo-ausbildung_vorbereiten-07.question: After eight months of training it emerges that the trainer named in the contract never held the professional suitability required by § 30 BBiG. What is the consequence for the training contract?

options.a: The contract is void from the outset; the training time completed does not count
options.b: The contract is valid until the objection is raised and ends automatically with it
options.c: The validity of the training contract is unaffected - a defect in the entitlement to take on or train apprentices does not affect it; the suitability defect must be remedied vis-à-vis the competent chamber
options.d: The contract retroactively converts into an employment relationship

aevo-ausbildung_vorbereiten-07.explanation: § 10(4) BBiG expressly protects apprentices against exactly this situation: "A defect in the entitlement to take on or to train apprentices does not affect the validity of the training contract." The apprentice is not to bear the consequences of the company failing to meet its suitability requirements - training time, the right to an allowance, and the prospect of sitting the examination all remain intact. So (a), (b) and (d) are wrong. The consequence hits the company at the supervisory level: the chamber supervises suitability under § 76(1) BBiG and can demand that defects be remedied, and under § 29 no. 2 BBiG repeated or serious contravention can even remove personal suitability. In practice, a suitable trainer must be appointed without delay under § 28(2) BBiG.

aevo-ausbildung_vorbereiten-08.question: Three small craft businesses want to train jointly, because none of them can cover all the content alone. How is this classified legally?

options.a: Each business concludes its own training contract for each training phase
options.b: Consortium training under § 10(5) BBiG: several natural or legal persons cooperate in fulfilling the contractual obligations, as long as responsibility for the individual training phases and for the training period as a whole is assured
options.c: Permissible only with an exemption from the Federal Institute for Vocational Education and Training
options.d: Not permissible - training may only take place in a single establishment

aevo-ausbildung_vorbereiten-08.explanation: § 10(5) BBiG expressly governs consortium training: "Several natural or legal persons may cooperate in a training consortium to fulfil the training provider's contractual obligations, as far as responsibility for the individual training phases and for the training period as a whole is assured." There is still ONE training contract with one training provider - which is why (a) is wrong. No BIBB exemption (c) is required; BIBB participates in regulatory procedures and its main committee can adopt recommendations. (d) is the opposite of the legal position: § 27(2) BBiG expressly deems an establishment that cannot deliver everything suitable if the missing content is delivered elsewhere, and § 3(1) no. 5 AEVO makes exactly that assessment a trainer competence. The establishment and any measures outside it must be entered in the contract record under § 11(1) sentence 2 no. 4 BBiG.

aevo-ausbildung_vorbereiten-09.question: An applicant with caring responsibilities asks whether she can do the training part-time. What applies under § 7a BBiG?

options.a: Part-time training is only possible where a legitimate interest exists and the chamber consents
options.b: Part-time training is only permitted for the second half of the training
options.c: Training may be delivered part-time; the reduction in daily or weekly training time must be agreed in the contract and may not exceed 50 percent, with the duration extending accordingly - up to at most one and a half times the full-time duration
options.d: Part-time training never extends the training duration, because the same content is delivered

aevo-ausbildung_vorbereiten-09.explanation: § 7a(1) BBiG makes part-time training available without preconditions: it "may" be delivered, the contract must agree the reduction of daily or weekly training time for the whole or a defined period, and the reduction may not exceed 50 percent. Since the reform, the provision no longer requires a legitimate interest or an approval - (a) is outdated. § 7a(2) BBiG governs the consequence: the duration extends accordingly, but at most to one and a half times the full-time duration, rounded down to whole months - so (d) is wrong. Under para. 3 the duration extends, at the apprentice's request, even beyond that maximum until the next possible final examination. There is no restriction to the second half as in (b). Practically relevant: under § 7a(4) BBiG the registration application can be combined with a shortening application under § 8(1) BBiG, and § 17(5) BBiG permits a proportionate reduction of the allowance - but not a steeper one than the reduction in working time.

aevo-ausbildung_vorbereiten-10.question: An applicant has an intermediate school-leaving certificate and has already completed a year of a related apprenticeship. You want to shorten the training duration. What is the correct route?

options.a: The company sets the shortened duration in the contract; no third party needs to be involved
options.b: The apprentice applies for the shortening alone at the vocational school
options.c: The shortening follows automatically from the school-leaving certificate, without an application
options.d: Apprentice and training provider make a joint application to the competent chamber; the chamber must shorten the duration where it is to be expected that the training goal will be reached in the shortened time

aevo-ausbildung_vorbereiten-10.explanation: § 8(1) sentence 1 BBiG ties shortening to two elements: a JOINT application by apprentice and training provider, and the forecast that the training goal will be reached in the shortened time. Where both are present, the chamber "must" shorten - it is a bound decision, not a discretion, but it rests with the chamber and not the company. So (a) and (c) are wrong, and (b) names both the wrong applicant and the wrong body. For calculating the reduction, the BIBB main committee may adopt recommendations under § 8(3) BBiG - that is where the customary credit values for school certificates and prior learning come from. This must be distinguished from extension under § 8(2) BBiG: apprentices apply for that alone, it lies in the chamber's discretion, and the training provider must be heard first. Neither should be confused with early admission to the final examination under § 45(1) BBiG, which leaves the training duration itself untouched.

aevo-ausbildung_vorbereiten-11.question: Your works council states that it considers the newly appointed trainer not suitable in vocational/work-pedagogical terms and demands their removal. What legal basis stands behind that?

options.a: § 29 BBiG - the works council determines personal suitability
options.b: § 98(2) BetrVG - the works council may object to the appointment of a person charged with delivering in-company vocational training, or demand their removal, where that person lacks personal or professional suitability - in particular the vocational/work-pedagogical suitability within the meaning of the BBiG - or neglects their duties
options.c: § 76 BBiG - the works council exercises supervision over training
options.d: There is no such power; the employer alone decides on the appointment

aevo-ausbildung_vorbereiten-11.explanation: § 98(2) BetrVG gives the works council a distinct right expressly tied to vocational/work-pedagogical suitability: objecting to the appointment or demanding removal where the commissioned person lacks personal or professional suitability within the meaning of the BBiG or neglects their duties. If no agreement is reached, the works council may apply to the labour court under § 98(5) BetrVG; if the employer disregards a final decision, an administrative fine (up to EUR 10,000) or a coercive penalty may follow. So (d) is wrong. § 29 BBiG (a) defines personal suitability but confers no determination power on the works council; § 76 BBiG (c) assigns supervision to the competent chamber, not the works council. Alongside these stand § 98(1) BetrVG (co-determination on the delivery of in-company training measures), § 97 BetrVG (consultation on facilities and measures, co-determination where measures change employees' duties) and § 96 BetrVG (promotion of vocational training) - § 3(2) no. 2 AEVO requires these rights to be taken into account.

aevo-ausbildung_vorbereiten-12.question: A 17-year-old applicant is to start her training on 1 August. Which condition must you mandatorily have satisfied before employment begins?

options.a: Written consent from the vocational school
options.b: A certificate from the chamber confirming the establishment's suitability for minors
options.c: A doctor's certificate confirming an initial medical examination carried out within the last 14 months
options.d: Nothing in particular - the Youth Employment Protection Act no longer applies to apprentices over 16

aevo-ausbildung_vorbereiten-12.explanation: § 32(1) JArbSchG permits employing a young person entering working life only if they have been medically examined within the last fourteen months (initial examination) AND the employer holds the certificate issued by that doctor. Both must therefore be in place BEFORE employment starts. A "young person" for the Act's purposes is someone aged 15 but not yet 18 - so (d) is wrong; § 15(3) BBiG expressly refers apprentices under 18 to the JArbSchG. Under § 33 JArbSchG a first follow-up examination follows a year later, and under its para. 3 the young person may not continue to be employed after 14 months have elapsed while the certificate is missing - which is exactly why the Rahmenplan names the "Voruntersuchung" in HF 2.5 as a contract-preparation topic. (a) and (b) do not exist as legal duties.

aevo-ausbildung_vorbereiten-13.question: Your technical department wants to publish the apprenticeship advert as "We are looking for a young, German-speaking junior mechanic (m)". How do you react?

options.a: Agree - the AGG does not yet apply to training places, because no employment relationship exists yet
options.b: Refuse, and redraft the advert around the actual job requirements and free of discrimination: the AGG expressly covers apprentices and applicants, and a position may not be advertised in breach of the anti-discrimination rule
options.c: Agree, if the wording is softened during the interview
options.d: Refuse, but only because of the masculine form; age and language are permissible criteria

aevo-ausbildung_vorbereiten-13.explanation: The AGG bites here at three levels. § 6(1) sentence 1 no. 2 AGG expressly counts "persons employed for their vocational training" as employees, and sentence 2 puts applicants on the same footing - so (a) is wrong. § 2(1) no. 1 AGG covers selection criteria and hiring conditions, and no. 3 additionally covers access to vocational training including apprenticeships. § 7(1) AGG prohibits disadvantage on the grounds listed in § 1 AGG - including sex, age and ethnic origin - and § 11 AGG expressly prohibits advertising a position in breach of § 7(1) AGG. The example wording breaches this three times over: "young" (age), "German-speaking" (ethnic origin, unless genuinely job-related) and "(m)" (sex). Softening it in the interview (c) does not cure the advertising breach; under § 15(2) AGG rejected applicants can claim compensation. (d) underestimates age and language. The Rahmenplan names exactly this combination in HF 2.4: "planning and conducting selection procedures taking account of the General Equal Treatment Act and the GDPR" and "addressing applicants appropriately for the target group and free of stereotypes".

aevo-ausbildung_vorbereiten-14.question: A second-year apprentice in a three-year apprenticeship wants to spend three months at a partner company in Spain. What must be observed legally?

options.a: Periods abroad are only possible after the training has been completed
options.b: The period abroad interrupts the training relationship; no allowance is payable for that time
options.c: Parts of the training may be delivered abroad where this serves the training goal; the total duration should not exceed a quarter of the training duration set in the training regulation, and for anything longer than eight weeks a plan agreed with the competent chamber is required
options.d: Periods abroad are possible without limit, as long as the partner company is professionally suitable

aevo-ausbildung_vorbereiten-14.explanation: § 2(3) BBiG expressly permits periods abroad: "Parts of the vocational training may be delivered abroad where this serves the training goal. Their total duration should not exceed a quarter of the training duration set in the training regulation." For a three-year apprenticeship that is roughly nine months - so three months is within range, and (a) is wrong. § 76(3) BBiG adds the procedural side: the chamber supervises and promotes delivery, and "where a training phase abroad lasts more than eight weeks, a plan agreed with the competent chamber is required for it". That also makes (d) wrong. The training relationship continues throughout - the period abroad is part of the training, not an interruption of it, so the duty to pay under § 17(1) BBiG persists and (b) is wrong. § 3(2) no. 6 AEVO makes assessing this option a trainer competence; the Rahmenplan additionally names mobility advice, funding programmes and leave from vocational school in HF 2.6.

aevo-ausbildung_vorbereiten-15.question: You notice that the vocational school only covers a learning field in the third year of training, which your company already uses in practice in the first year. What is the appropriate response in terms of Handlungsfeld 2?

options.a: Postpone the company-side deployment to the third year so that school and company run in sync
options.b: Use learning-venue cooperation: talk to the vocational school, align goals and content across the two venues, and design the company-side delivery so that the school knowledge can later build on it
options.c: Ask the competent chamber to adapt the school framework curriculum
options.d: Do nothing - company and vocational school are legally separate venues with no need for coordination

aevo-ausbildung_vorbereiten-15.explanation: § 3(2) no. 3 AEVO requires "identifying the need for cooperation and coordinating substantively and organisationally with cooperation partners, in particular the vocational school". § 2(2) BBiG names the principle: the learning venues "cooperate in delivering vocational training (learning-venue cooperation)" - so (d) is wrong. The 2023 Rahmenplan spells out in HF 2.3 "ensuring learning-venue cooperation between company and vocational school" and names the alignment of goals and content across venues. (a) sacrifices the company's process logic to a false synchrony - the company is bound to its work and business processes, not to the school's chronology, and § 3(2) no. 1 AEVO requires precisely that process orientation. (c) confuses competences: school framework curricula rest on state law and standing-conference decisions, not on any chamber power.

aevo-ausbildung_vorbereiten-16.question: Your company wants to take on a student as an intern for six months to give her occupational experience - it is not a vocational training relationship within the meaning of the BBiG, and no employment relationship is agreed. Which rules apply?

options.a: None of the BBiG's rules - the Act only applies to recognised training occupations
options.b: The BBiG applies in full, including the registration duty and the final examination
options.c: § 26 BBiG makes §§ 10 to 16, § 17(1), (6) and (7), §§ 18 to 23 and § 25 BBiG applicable - with the proviso that the statutory probationary period may be shortened, the written contract record may be dispensed with, and no damages may be claimed for early termination after probation
options.d: Only the Minimum Wage Act applies

aevo-ausbildung_vorbereiten-16.explanation: § 26 BBiG covers "other contractual relationships": persons taken on to acquire occupational skills, knowledge, abilities or experience without this being vocational training within the meaning of the Act - and without an employment relationship being agreed. For them, §§ 10 to 16 and § 17(1), (6) and (7) as well as §§ 18 to 23 and § 25 BBiG expressly apply, but with three provisos: the statutory probationary period may be shortened, the written contract record may be dispensed with, and for early termination after probation no damages may be claimed, deviating from § 23(1) sentence 1 BBiG. So (a) is too broad and (b) too broad in the other direction: registration (§ 36 BBiG) and the examination regime (§§ 37 ff. BBiG) are precisely not on the list. (d) leaves the BBiG out entirely. Practically important: the duty to pay under § 17(1) BBiG IS on the list - an unpaid relationship of this kind is therefore not compatible with it.

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-01.question: You are planning a training unit and formulating the learning objective. Which wording is operationalised, i.e. verifiable?

options.a: The apprentice should understand the importance of quality assurance
options.b: The apprentice should develop a feel for clean work
options.c: By the end of the unit, the apprentice can independently mark out and centre-punch five workpieces from a drawing, with a dimensional deviation not exceeding 0.5 mm
options.d: The apprentice should be made familiar with the basics of marking out

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-01.explanation: The Rahmenplan expressly requires, in HF 3.3, "formulating, concretising and verifying learning objectives" - verifiability is built in, not optional. An operationalised (fine-grained) objective names three elements: the observable end behaviour ("mark out and centre-punch", with an observable verb rather than "understand" or "be made familiar with"), the conditions ("independently, from a drawing") and the standard of assessment ("five workpieces", "deviation no more than 0.5 mm"). Only (c) contains all three. (a) and (d) use non-observable verbs - "understand" and "be made familiar with" cannot be verified and are therefore unusable as a fine-grained objective (they are fine as broad or intermediate objectives, but must be concretised for delivery). (b) describes an attitude with no standard at all. Practical payoff: only an operationalised objective can be checked at the end of the unit by a performance check in the sense of HF 3.8 - and in the practical exam's Fachgespräch, objective formulation is one of the criteria.

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-02.question: You want to teach an apprentice how to correctly attach a load to a crane. Which learning domain does this objective mainly belong to, and what follows from that for the choice of method?

options.a: Cognitive domain - a technical talk with a handout is sufficient
options.b: Psychomotor domain - the sequence of movements must be demonstrated, imitated and practised; a talk alone is not enough
options.c: Affective domain - what matters is that the apprentice accepts safety as a value
options.d: The learning domain is irrelevant to the choice of method; only the apprentice's stage of training matters

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-02.explanation: The Rahmenplan names "objective levels, learning domains" as example content in HF 3.3 and expressly requires in HF 3.4 "describing criteria for selecting methods and justifying the choice of method" - the learning domain is one of those criteria, which is why (d) is wrong. The three customary domains are cognitive (knowledge, comprehension, application), psychomotor (movement sequences, manual skills) and affective (attitudes, values, dispositions). Attaching a load is primarily a movement skill performed under safety constraints, hence psychomotor: such objectives require demonstration, imitation and practice - classically the four-step method. A talk alone (a) misses the domain; crane work of course also has cognitive elements (reading the load chart, selecting slings) and an affective element (c) in the sense of safety awareness - but the load-bearing skill is motor. Remember the pattern: clarify the objective and its domain first, then choose the method, never the other way round.

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-03.question: You are instructing using the four-step method. What is the correct order of the four steps?

options.a: Explain - question - practise - check
options.b: Demonstrate - explain - imitate - praise
options.c: Motivate - inform - apply - assess
options.d: Prepare (step 1) - trainer demonstrates and explains (step 2) - apprentice imitates and explains (step 3) - practise and consolidate with a performance check (step 4)

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-03.explanation: The Rahmenplan names the four-step method in HF 3.4 as one of the activity-promoting methods and requires presenting and carrying out its possible applications. The classic sequence is: (1) prepare - ready the workstation, material and apprentice, state the objective, motivate and connect to prior knowledge; (2) demonstrate and explain - the trainer works through it slowly and explains the key points; (3) imitate and explain - the apprentice performs the task AND explains what they are doing, so that comprehension errors become visible, not just execution errors; (4) practise and consolidate - independent practice, performance check, feedback, transfer into everyday work. (b) omits step 1 and reduces the apprentice's explaining to mere praise. (a) and (c) are invented sequences. Important exam note for the practical part: under some chambers' guidance, this conventional method is expressly excluded as the subject of the "presentation" option, because a longer self-directed training unit is to be shown there - whereas for the "practical execution" option in industrial/technical occupations it is the standard case. Always check this point in your own chamber's information sheet; it is chamber practice, not an AEVO requirement.

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-04.question: For your presentation in the practical part of the exam, you want to describe a self-directed training unit using the model of the complete action. Which sequence of steps does that mean?

options.a: Observe - imitate - repeat - master
options.b: Inform - plan - decide - carry out - check - assess/reflect
options.c: Analyse - document - present - archive
options.d: Introduction - main part - conclusion - performance check

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-04.explanation: The model of the complete action is expressly named in the Rahmenplan under HF 3.3 as a didactic principle ("didactic principles, e.g. linking learning and working, learning in real operational processes, model of the complete action, learning by teaching") and is at the same time the reference structure of the guiding-text method. The six steps are: inform (grasp the task, gather information), plan (steps, material, time), decide (agree the plan with the trainer, weigh alternatives), carry out (work independently), check (test the result against the specification, ideally oneself) and assess/reflect (debrief, transfer to the next task). Crucially, planning, deciding and checking lie with the apprentice - that is precisely the difference from the four-step method, in which the trainer leads the demonstration and the assessment. (a) roughly describes an imitation sequence, (c) a documentation procedure, (d) the formal structure of an instruction lesson - none of these is the model of the complete action.

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-05.question: A third-year apprentice is to introduce a new inspection fixture within the team. Which method is best justified here on professional grounds?

options.a: The four-step method, because it is always the safest choice
options.b: A short talk by the trainer, because that is the fastest form of delivery
options.c: A learning assignment or another task-oriented method with learning-process guidance, because the stage of training and the objective require independent planning, deciding and checking
options.d: A role play, because teamwork is the focus

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-05.explanation: The Rahmenplan requires in HF 3.4 not only knowledge of methods but expressly "describing criteria for selecting methods and justifying the choice", and names as criteria the objectives, learning prerequisites, stage of training, framework conditions, developmental phase, cultural and social context, and learning venues. It also highlights "competence-promoting and business-process-oriented training methods, in particular learning-process guidance". For a third-year apprentice and an objective encompassing planning, deciding and checking, a learning assignment with learning-process guidance is the defensible choice. (a) is the classic mistake: the four-step method is strong for psychomotor skills and weak prior knowledge; here it would under-challenge the apprentice and strip out precisely the planning and decision-making elements. (b) confuses efficiency of delivery with effectiveness of learning. (d) would fit if the objective lay in communication behaviour - here it lies in the technical introduction of a fixture. "There is no best method, only one that fits the objective" is the core statement expected in the exam.

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-06.question: An apprentice reliably completes routine tasks but shows little initiative and waits for every instruction. Which measure best matches the competence goal "create learning-conducive conditions and a motivating learning culture"?

options.a: Break the tasks down even further, so no uncertainty arises
options.b: Agree learning objectives jointly, widen scope for action and responsibility step by step, teach learning and working techniques, and give regular feedback - intrinsic motivation grows with experienced competence and self-efficacy
options.c: Offer a bonus for every task completed independently
options.d: Document the behaviour as a performance shortfall in the next appraisal and wait

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-06.explanation: § 3(3) no. 1 AEVO names the competence to "create learning-conducive conditions and a motivating learning culture, and to give and receive feedback". The Rahmenplan fleshes this out in HF 3.1 with "supporting the development of a culture of self-directed learning", "supporting learning processes through objective agreements, strengthening motivation and securing transfer", "promoting learning by teaching learning and working techniques", and with regular feedback; as example content it expressly names "foundations of motivation, e.g. learning motives, intrinsic and extrinsic motivation". (a) reinforces the very dependency that is the problem. (c) relies solely on extrinsic motivation through a material incentive - effective short-term, but it builds no intrinsic motivation and can even crowd it out. (d) confuses appraisal with development: under HF 3.8, performance assessment exists to "draw conclusions for the further course of training", not to wait and see.

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-07.question: You are giving an apprentice feedback on a failed assembly. Which of the following feedback rules are professionally correct? (3 correct answers)

options.a: Concrete and descriptive, relating to observable behaviour rather than to the person
options.b: Ideally bundled at the end of the training year, so that individual incidents are not overweighted
options.c: Close in time to the event, one-to-one, and in a situation where the apprentice is receptive
options.d: Conducted as a dialogue: first ask for the apprentice's own assessment, then add your own perception, then agree next steps together
options.e: Together with at least three further criticisms, so the apprentice gets an overall picture

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-07.explanation: The Rahmenplan expressly names, in HF 3.1, "forms and necessity of feedback, e.g. reflection conversations, feedback rules", and requires making the apprentice's "competence development clear through regular feedback" as well as receiving feedback from apprentices - feedback is therefore two-way, which is why (d) is correct. The recognised rules are: prompt, concrete and behaviour-related (not person-related: "the bolted joint was not tightened to the specified torque" rather than "you're sloppy"), descriptive rather than judgemental, one-to-one where critical, dialogic, and closing with a concrete agreement on the next step. (b) breaches promptness and renders feedback ineffective - a year later the learning occasion is forgotten; the Rahmenplan expressly demands regular feedback. (e) overloads the conversation: several criticisms at once overwhelm and bury the one point that could change behaviour. The Rahmenplan additionally names "error culture" as example content in HF 3.1 - errors are an occasion for learning, not primarily for sanctions.

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-08.question: You are scheduling a demanding new instruction session into the working day. Taking the daily performance curve into account, which slot is most favourable?

options.a: Immediately after the lunch break, because the apprentices are then rested
options.b: Late afternoon, because that is when the workplace is quietest
options.c: Late morning, in the day's first performance peak - the trough typically falls in the early afternoon hours
options.d: The time of day is irrelevant to learning performance; only the method matters

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-08.explanation: The Rahmenplan expressly names "daily performance curve, fatigue and recovery" as example content in HF 3.1 and requires "ensuring external learning-conducive conditions" - the time of day is therefore part of training planning and not a matter of indifference, which is why (d) is wrong. The typical daily performance curve shows a first peak in the late morning, a marked trough in the early afternoon, and a second, lower peak in the early evening. Demanding first-time delivery therefore belongs in the morning peak; the afternoon trough is better suited to practice, revision and routine work. (a) hits the trough precisely. (b) confuses a quiet workplace with personal capacity - the two can diverge. In addition, the external conditions under HF 3.1 include the organisational, spatial, temporal and digital learning environment - and, legally, the limits on rest breaks for young people in § 11 JArbSchG.

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-09.question: How do you design the probationary period properly in terms of Handlungsfeld 3?

options.a: As an observation phase without any special measures - the real training only starts after probation
options.b: As pure familiarisation within one department, to avoid friction
options.c: With a single closing conversation at the end, so the judgement stays uninfluenced
options.d: Deliberately: onboarding and induction into the company, occupation-typical learning and work tasks that yield evidence of aptitude and inclination, induction and appraisal conversations along the way, documented assessment, and consequences drawn from it before probation ends

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-09.explanation: § 3(3) no. 2 AEVO uses three verbs: "to organise, to design and to assess" the probationary period - it is therefore expressly a design task, not waiting time, which is why (a) and (b) miss the competence goal. The 2023 Rahmenplan spells out in HF 3.2: "planning and carrying out onboarding and induction of apprentices into the company", "assessing the development of the apprentice's learning and working behaviour during probation and discussing it with them, drawing consequences where appropriate", and "observing the legal basis of probation"; as example content it names occupational safety, company information, corporate culture, retention measures such as buddy and mentoring schemes, and "occupation-typical learning and work tasks for systematically establishing aptitude and inclination". (c) is also legally risky: probation lasts at most four months under § 20 BBiG, and only within that time may either side terminate at any time without notice under § 22(1) BBiG - anyone who defers the assessment to the final day has no time left to draw consequences or trial supporting measures.

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-10.question: In the third month of probation it becomes clear that an apprentice is evidently not suited to the occupation. How can the training relationship be ended?

options.a: Only with four weeks' notice and stating the reasons
options.b: At any time without observing a notice period - but the termination must be in written form; electronic form is excluded
options.c: Only for good cause, because the BBiG provides special protection against dismissal
options.d: Only with the consent of the competent chamber

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-10.explanation: § 22(1) BBiG: "During the probationary period the training relationship may be terminated at any time without observing a notice period." Neither good cause, nor a notice period, nor third-party consent is required - (a), (c) and (d) are wrong. What matters is the form: § 22(3) BBiG requires written form and expressly excludes electronic form, so a termination by email is ineffective. Reasons must be stated only in the cases of paragraph 2 (i.e. after probation), not during probation. Two traps: probation lasts at most four months under § 20 BBiG, and for minors the termination must reach the legal representatives. Where a works council exists, § 102 BetrVG must also be observed. Professionally, a documented conversation with supporting measures should precede any probation termination - the Rahmenplan expressly requires in HF 3.2 "drawing consequences where appropriate" and "pointing out alternative perspectives".

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-11.question: A second-year apprentice demonstrably stole tools three weeks ago; management learned of it the same day and now wants to dismiss without notice. How do you assess this?

options.a: Permissible - theft is always good cause, and no time limit applies to it
options.b: Permissible, if the termination is delivered by email with a read receipt
options.c: Not permissible - after probation, only the apprentice may terminate
options.d: Ineffective: a termination for good cause is ineffective if the facts underlying it have been known to the person entitled to terminate for more than two weeks - that deadline has passed

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-11.explanation: § 22(4) sentence 1 BBiG contains a cut-off period: "A termination for good cause is ineffective if the facts underlying it have been known to the person entitled to terminate for more than two weeks." After three weeks' knowledge, extraordinary termination is therefore barred - regardless of how serious the breach was. That is why (a) is wrong: good cause alone is not enough, the deadline must be met. Sentence 2 suspends the running of the period only where a designated conciliation procedure before an out-of-court body has been initiated - typically a conciliation committee under § 111(2) ArbGG. (b) fails on form: § 22(3) BBiG requires written form and excludes electronic form; moreover, in the cases of paragraph 2 the ground for termination must be stated. (c) is wrong, but compresses a correct core: after probation, § 22(2) BBiG allows termination without notice only for good cause - a termination on four weeks' notice is available only to apprentices, and only where they give up the training or want to train for a different occupation.

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-12.question: A second-year apprentice terminates with four weeks' notice because she wants to give up the apprenticeship and go to university. Your management wants to claim damages for the wasted training expenditure. What applies?

options.a: Damages are possible, because the apprentice is responsible for the ground of dissolution
options.b: A damages claim is excluded: § 23(1) sentence 2 BBiG expressly exempts precisely the case of termination under § 22(2) no. 2 BBiG
options.c: Damages are possible but capped at three months' allowance
options.d: Damages are possible if asserted within three months

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-12.explanation: § 22(2) no. 2 BBiG gives apprentices their own right to terminate on four weeks' notice where they want to give up the training or train for a different occupation. § 23(1) sentence 1 BBiG in principle grants a damages claim on early dissolution after probation where the other side is responsible for the ground of dissolution - but sentence 2 expressly exempts the case of § 22(2) no. 2 BBiG. Freedom of occupational choice is not to be burdened with compensation claims; so (a), (c) and (d) are wrong. The three-month period mentioned in (d) does exist, though: § 23(2) BBiG extinguishes the claim if it is not asserted within three months of the end of the relationship - it is the cut-off for those cases where a claim exists at all, e.g. conduct-based extraordinary termination by the company. The three-months'-pay cap in (c) comes from § 15(2) AGG and has nothing to do with § 23 BBiG. In addition, § 12(2) no. 1 BBiG voids any repayment agreement on training costs in any event.

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-13.question: For some weeks an apprentice has seemed unfocused, makes mistakes on tasks he previously mastered, and has withdrawn. What is the professionally correct first step?

options.a: Issue a written warning for declining performance
options.b: Immediately apply for training-accompanying support from the employment agency
options.c: Describe the manifestation, explore possible causes in a learning-needs conversation, and check the learning prerequisites - only then choose the appropriate measure
options.d: Extend the training period by six months as a precaution

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-13.explanation: § 3(3) no. 5 AEVO requires supporting apprentices with learning difficulties "through individual design of the training and learning advice, deploying training-support assistance where needed, and examining the possibility of extending the training period" - in that order. The 2023 Rahmenplan sets out the diagnostic steps in HF 3.5: "recognising learning difficulties and establishing possible causes", "checking the learning prerequisites", "offering advice and individual assistance where difficulties arise", and ONLY THEN "recognising the need for training-accompanying support and organising measures" and "examining options for adjusting training time and duration". As causes it expressly names over- and under-challenge, personality-related factors, health and cognitive impairments, external factors, dysfunctional learning behaviour and disinterest - a drop in performance on previously mastered tasks precisely does not indicate a lack of ability. (a) sanctions a symptom whose cause is unknown. (b) and (d) skip the diagnosis and put the measure before the cause; extension under § 8(2) BBiG requires an application from the apprentice in any case.

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-14.question: After a long illness, an apprentice has missed a substantial training phase; the examination is in five months. You are considering extending the training period. What is the correct route?

options.a: Company and apprentice agree the extension in the contract; no third party needs to be involved
options.b: The apprentice applies to the competent chamber; in exceptional cases the chamber may extend the period where the extension is necessary to reach the training goal - the training provider must be heard before the decision
options.c: The company applies; the apprentice must be heard
options.d: An extension is only possible after a failed final examination

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-14.explanation: § 8(2) BBiG: "In exceptional cases the competent chamber may, on application by the apprentice, extend the training duration where the extension is necessary to reach the training goal. Before deciding on the extension, the training provider must be heard." Three points matter for the exam: the applicants are the apprentices alone (which is why (c) is wrong - unlike shortening under § 8(1) BBiG, the right to apply is precisely not joint here), the decision rests with the chamber and lies in its discretion ("may", "exceptional cases"), and the training provider has a right to be heard but no veto. A mere contractual agreement as in (a) is not enough - the training duration follows the training regulation (§ 5(1) no. 2 BBiG), from which only the chamber may deviate. (d) confuses two different instruments: extension under § 8(2) BBiG (during training, on application, discretionary) and the automatic extension under § 21(3) BBiG after a failed final examination (at the apprentice's request, until the next possible resit, by at most one year).

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-15.question: A high-performing apprentice is well ahead of her cohort's training level and wants to sit the examination earlier. Which route fits and what must be observed?

options.a: The company simply registers her for the earlier examination date; there are no further conditions
options.b: Only shortening the training duration under § 8(1) BBiG is available; there is no such thing as early admission
options.c: Early admission to the final examination under § 45(1) BBiG: it is possible where her performance justifies it - after hearing the training provider and the vocational school; the chamber decides
options.d: An early examination is only permissible where the final examination is split into two parts

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-15.explanation: § 45(1) BBiG: "After hearing the training provider and the vocational school, apprentices may be admitted to the final examination before the end of their training period where their performance justifies it." Three features: a performance condition, a double hearing (company AND vocational school), and a decision by the chamber - admission is decided by the chamber under § 46(1) BBiG, not by the company, which is why (a) is wrong. (b) overlooks that there are two distinct instruments: shortening the training duration under § 8(1) BBiG (joint application, changes the contract duration) and early admission under § 45(1) BBiG (does not change the training duration but brings the examination date forward; if the apprentice passes, the relationship ends under § 21(2) BBiG on announcement of the result). (d) invents a condition. § 3(3) no. 6 AEVO requires examining both options, and the Rahmenplan additionally names, in HF 3.6, additional qualifications, more responsible tasks and further-training advice as development offers for high performers - as well as expressly "shaping the remaining training duration where the period is shortened".

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-16.question: Two apprentices repeatedly clash; the team atmosphere suffers and each blames the other. How do you proceed as the trainer?

options.a: Do not intervene - conflicts among apprentices are best resolved among peers
options.b: Intervene early, analyse the conflict (type, escalation stage, underlying interests), first hold individual conversations, then a facilitated joint conversation ending in a concrete, verifiable agreement
options.c: Give both a reprimand and permanently separate their workstations
options.d: Ask the works council to resolve the conflict, since you lack the competence

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-16.explanation: § 3(3) no. 7 AEVO frames the competence as a chain: promote social and personal development, "recognise problems and conflicts in good time and work towards a solution". "In good time" rules out the wait-and-see of (a) - the higher the escalation stage, the lower the chance of a solution without third parties. The 2023 Rahmenplan expressly names, in HF 3.7, "recognising conspicuous behaviour and conflict situations in training in good time, analysing them, and applying strategies for handling conflict constructively", with the example content "types of conflict, e.g. individual conflicts, group conflicts", "conflict-resolution competence, e.g. escalation stages, conciliation options" and "handling contradictions, e.g. conflicts of interest and goals" - exactly the analytical steps in (b). (c) treats the symptom: physical separation ends the friction but does not resolve the conflict, and denies both the chance to learn how to handle conflict. (d) misreads your role - the works council has participation rights in vocational training under §§ 96-98 BetrVG but is not a conflict facilitator in the trainer's place. The Rahmenplan additionally requires in HF 3.7 "reflecting on the causes of training dropout and taking measures to avoid it" - unresolved conflict is among the most common of those causes.

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-17.question: You are appraising an apprentice who is an exceptionally strong presenter. As a result her care, resilience and technical knowledge are also rated above average in the appraisal, although you have no concrete observations to support that. Which appraisal error is this?

options.a: Contrast error
options.b: "Nikolaus" (recency) effect
options.c: Halo effect: one salient individual characteristic colours the assessment of all the others
options.d: First-impression error

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-17.explanation: The Rahmenplan expressly names, in HF 3.8, "appraisal errors, e.g. first impression, recency ("Nikolaus") effect, halo effect, contrast error", and requires avoiding them. They are clearly distinguishable: the halo effect occurs when a single salient characteristic - positive or negative - outshines the assessment of all the others; that is exactly what the case describes. The recency effect over-weights the most recently observed performance because it is best remembered at the end of the appraisal period. The first-impression error lets an early perception shape the entire later course. The contrast error arises from comparison with a person appraised immediately beforehand instead of with the objective standard of requirements. The remedies are organisational: criteria-based appraisal forms with separately rated characteristics, ongoing behaviour documentation across the whole period rather than recall on the cut-off date, multi-rater appraisal, and comparison against the training regulation's requirements rather than against other apprentices.

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-18.question: You are developing a performance check for a training phase. Which basic requirements does the Rahmenplan set for performance checks? (3 correct answers)

options.a: Validity - the check actually measures what the learning objective states
options.b: Objectivity and transparency - the result is independent of the assessor, and the criteria are known to apprentices beforehand
options.c: Anonymity - the check is carried out without names
options.d: Reliability and economy - the check yields comparable results on repetition and involves a defensible amount of effort
options.e: Comparability with the result of the person appraised most recently

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-18.explanation: The Rahmenplan names, in HF 3.8, "basic requirements for performance checks, e.g. validity, reliability, objectivity, transparency, economy" - every criterion in (a), (b) and (d) appears there. Translated: validity means the check measures the behaviour stated in the objective - a written question does not test a psychomotor objective. Reliability means a repetition under the same conditions yields the same result. Objectivity means independence from the assessor. Transparency means apprentices know the criteria and the standard in advance. Economy keeps the effort within defensible limits. Anonymity (c) is not one of these requirements - an individual performance assessment in training necessarily presupposes attribution to a person, because § 3(3) no. 8 AEVO requires "conclusions for the further course of training" to be drawn from it. (e) practically describes the contrast error that the same Rahmenplan section requires you to avoid: the yardstick is the requirements, not other people.

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-19.question: You are holding a half-yearly appraisal conversation. How do you structure it properly?

options.a: You read out the completed appraisal form and have it signed
options.b: You start with the weaknesses so there is enough time for criticism, and close with a compliment
options.c: You first have the apprentice self-assess, then place your criteria-based observations alongside, work through the divergences together, and agree verifiable objectives for the next period
options.d: You skip preparation so that the conversation stays open and unprejudiced

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-19.explanation: § 3(3) no. 8 AEVO sets out the full chain: establish and assess performance, evaluate third-party assessments and examination results, "conduct appraisal conversations", and "draw conclusions for the further course of training". The conversation is therefore part of a feedback loop and not an act of announcement - which is why (a) is wrong. The 2023 Rahmenplan expressly names self-assessment as a form of performance check in HF 3.8 and requires "appraising the apprentice's learning behaviour regularly and against criteria" and "conducting learning-needs conversations and deriving measures from them" - exactly the structure in (c). Putting the self-assessment first has a practical reason: it surfaces differences in perception and activates the apprentice rather than pushing them into a defensive posture. (b) is the mechanical "sandwich" that is seen through quickly and dilutes the substance. (d) breaches the transparency and objectivity requirements for performance checks in the same Rahmenplan section: without documented observations you assess from memory and run straight into the appraisal errors HF 3.8 tells you to avoid.

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-20.question: Your training cohort brings together apprentices of very different origins, religions and first languages. What does the competence goal "promote intercultural competences" require of you?

options.a: Consistently avoid raising cultural differences in day-to-day training, so that nobody is singled out
options.b: Meet all cultural backgrounds openly, take up culturally rooted differences positively, convey appreciation with regard to social diversity, and actively support apprentices in developing intercultural competences themselves
