options.c: Group apprentices by language so that communication is easier
options.d: Hand intercultural topics to an external trainer, because they are not part of the trainer's role

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-20.explanation: § 3(3) no. 9 AEVO makes "promoting intercultural competences" a distinct, standalone competence goal of Handlungsfeld 3 - it is therefore expressly a trainer task and not delegable, which is why (d) is wrong. The 2023 Rahmenplan sets out three sub-competences in HF 3.9: "meeting all cultural backgrounds openly, taking up culturally rooted differences positively", "conveying appreciation of others with regard to social diversity", and "supporting apprentices in developing intercultural competences"; as example content it names tolerance, constructive cooperation, empathy, respectful conduct, matter-of-factness, and "dimensions of diversity in working life, e.g. ethnic origin and nationality, religion and worldview". "Taking up positively" is the core: differences are named and made usable, not blanked out - so (a) is wrong. (c) produces segregation instead of cooperation and runs directly counter to the competence goal; the Rahmenplan expressly calls heterogeneity a "chance" in HF 3.1.

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-21.question: An apprentice has not submitted a training record for months. Whose duties are engaged, and what is the consequence?

options.a: Only the apprentice's - the company has nothing to do with the record
options.b: Only the company's - it must keep the record for the apprentice
options.c: Both: the apprentice must keep a written or electronic training record, and the training provider must require them to do so and review it regularly; without a submitted training record, one of the conditions for admission to the final examination is missing
options.d: Neither - the training record has been voluntary since the BBiG reform

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-21.explanation: The training record is a twofold duty. § 13 sentence 2 no. 7 BBiG obliges apprentices to "keep a written or electronic training record". § 14(2) BBiG obliges training providers to "require" them to do so "and to review it regularly", and to give them the opportunity to keep the record at the workplace. So (a), (b) and (d) are all wrong. The sanction bites at the end of training: § 43(1) no. 2 BBiG makes submitting a training record under § 13 sentence 2 no. 7 BBiG "via the training provider" a condition for admission to the final examination - if it is missing, admission can fail. The form of the record must appear in the contract record under § 11(1) sentence 2 no. 12 BBiG. The Rahmenplan additionally treats the record as a training instrument in HF 3.8: "using training records, including digital ones, for monitoring and support and for comparison with the training plan" - the regular review is therefore not a formality but your running reconciliation between plan and reality.

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-22.question: Your company wants to charge apprentices for prescribed technical literature and for the tools needed for the final examination. How do you assess this?

options.a: Permissible if agreed in the training contract
options.b: Not permissible: training means - in particular tools, materials and technical literature - required for the training and for sitting the interim and final examinations must be provided to apprentices free of charge
options.c: Permissible for apprentices of full age
options.d: Permissible up to 10 percent of the monthly training allowance

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-22.explanation: § 14(1) no. 3 BBiG obliges training providers to "provide apprentices free of charge with the training means, in particular tools, materials and technical literature, that are required for the training and for sitting interim and final examinations, including where these take place after the end of the training relationship". The clause on examinations after the relationship ends matters: the duty does not stop on the last day of training. Since the digitalisation reform, the same clause adds that the hardware and software additionally required for digital mobile training under § 28(2) sentence 2 BBiG must also be provided free. Deviating agreements are void under § 25 BBiG because they depart from this part of the Act to the apprentice's disadvantage; in addition, § 12(2) no. 1 BBiG expressly voids any obligation to pay compensation for the training. So (a), (c) and (d) are wrong - age, contract and percentage caps change nothing. Only means that are not "required" fall outside, e.g. personal equipment beyond what is needed.

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-23.question: Because a colleague is off sick, a first-year apprentice is to staff the mailroom continuously for three weeks and handle copying jobs. How do you assess this?

options.a: Permissible - every activity in the company serves the vocational training
options.b: Permissible if the apprentice agrees and the time is made up later
options.c: Not permissible: apprentices may only be assigned tasks that serve the purpose of the training and are appropriate to their physical strength - a three-week stand-in role unrelated to the training does not meet that
options.d: Not permissible, but only for minors

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-23.explanation: § 14(3) BBiG draws a hard line: "Apprentices may only be assigned tasks that serve the purpose of the training and are appropriate to their physical strength." The provision applies to all apprentices, regardless of age - so (d) is wrong. Together with § 14(1) no. 1 BBiG (systematic delivery, structured in time and substance, so the training goal can be reached within the planned period), the case becomes a double breach: a three-week stand-in role unrelated to training is neither training-purposive nor systematic. The apprentice's consent does not cure it, because § 25 BBiG voids agreements deviating to their disadvantage - so (b) is wrong, and (a) confuses business utility with training purpose. Brief involvement in simple tasks within normal operations is unproblematic; what is impermissible is sustained use as substitute labour. The competent chamber can object to such situations under its § 76 BBiG supervision; repeated or serious breaches can remove personal suitability under § 29 no. 2 BBiG.

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-24.question: For which of the following must you release apprentices from work under § 15 BBiG? (3 correct answers)

options.a: For attending vocational-school lessons
options.b: On a vocational-school day with more than five lessons of at least 45 minutes each, once per week
options.c: For the company Christmas party, because it serves social integration
options.d: On the working day immediately preceding the written final examination
options.e: For the entire week before the written final examination, for exam preparation

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-24.explanation: § 15(1) sentence 2 BBiG lists five cases of release: no. 1 attending vocational-school lessons; no. 2 on a school day with more than five lessons of at least 45 minutes each, once per week; no. 3 in school weeks with scheduled block teaching of at least 25 hours over at least five days (in which case additional company training events of up to two hours per week are permitted); no. 4 for attending examinations and training measures outside the establishment; and no. 5 on the working day immediately preceding the written final examination. Sentence 1 additionally prohibits employment before school lessons that start before 9 a.m. A whole preparation week (e) is not provided for - only the immediately preceding working day. A Christmas party (c) is not a release within the meaning of the provision. § 15(2) BBiG additionally governs how these periods count towards training time, and § 19(1) no. 1 BBiG the continued payment of the allowance. For apprentices under 18, § 15(3) BBiG applies the Youth Employment Protection Act in parallel - §§ 9 and 10 JArbSchG contain substantively corresponding rules.

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-25.question: A 17-year-old apprentice is to work from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. one day with a half-hour break. How do you assess this?

options.a: Permissible, because the weekly working time is complied with on average
options.b: Permissible if the apprentice agrees
options.c: Permissible, because the daily maximum working time for young people is ten hours
options.d: Not permissible on two counts: young people may not be employed for more than eight hours a day, and where working time exceeds six hours the rest breaks must total at least 60 minutes

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-25.explanation: Two provisions bite together. § 8(1) JArbSchG: young people may not be employed for more than eight hours a day and not more than 40 hours a week - the planned 9.5 working hours exceed that, which is why (c) is wrong (ten hours is the § 3 ArbZG limit for adults, not the JArbSchG limit). § 11(1) JArbSchG: rest breaks must total at least 30 minutes where working time exceeds 4.5 up to 6 hours and at least 60 minutes where it exceeds 6 hours; only an interruption of at least 15 minutes counts as a rest break. The half hour is therefore also too short. Averaging (a) does not help: the daily cap applies independently, and the exceptions in § 8(2) and (2a) JArbSchG permit at most 8.5 hours a day in narrow constellations. Consent (b) is irrelevant - the JArbSchG is mandatory occupational protection law. Note also § 11(2) JArbSchG: young people may not be employed for more than 4.5 hours consecutively without a break, and the break must fall no earlier than one hour after the start and no later than one hour before the end. Only a collective agreement may deviate, within narrow limits, under § 21a JArbSchG.

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-26.question: An apprentice is 16 years old at the start of the calendar year. What is the minimum paid holiday the company must grant him for that calendar year?

options.a: At least 20 working days - the statutory minimum under the Federal Holiday Act applies
options.b: At least 27 working days - the Youth Employment Protection Act grades the minimum holiday by age at the start of the calendar year
options.c: At least 30 working days - for all apprentices under 18
options.d: At least 24 working days

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-26.explanation: § 19(2) JArbSchG grades the minimum holiday by age at the start of the calendar year: at least 30 working days if the young person is not yet 16 at the start of the calendar year; at least 27 if not yet 17; at least 25 if not yet 18. A 16-year-old is "not yet 17" - so 27 working days. The grading requires careful reading: the cut-off is the start of the year, not the birthday, and the formula is "not yet", not "at least". The Federal Holiday Act's minimum (24 working days under § 3(1) BUrlG, not 20) takes second place here; § 19(4) JArbSchG refers to the BUrlG only for the remaining holiday questions - so (a) and (d) are wrong. (c) applies only to those under 16. Practically important for training planning is § 19(3) JArbSchG: holiday should be given to vocational-school students during the school holidays, and for every school day attended during the holiday an additional day of leave must be granted.

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-27.question: In your production area a group works on piece rates. A 17-year-old apprentice is to join in to get to know the process. What applies?

options.a: Permissible, because it serves the training
options.b: Permissible if the apprentice receives no piece-rate bonus
options.c: In principle prohibited: young people may not be employed on piecework nor in a work group with adult piece-rate workers - an exception for the group work applies only where this is necessary to achieve the training goal and protection is assured through the supervision of a competent person
options.d: Prohibited without any exception

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-27.explanation: § 23(1) JArbSchG prohibits three constellations: no. 1 piecework and other work where a higher wage can be earned through an increased work pace; no. 2 employment in a work group with adult employees engaged on such work; no. 3 work in which the pace is prescribed, set or enforced more than occasionally. The ban protects against pace pressure - which is why (b) does not help: joining the piece-rate group is already prohibited, regardless of the apprentice's own pay. § 23(2) JArbSchG does contain a precisely delimited exception, applying solely to paragraph 1 no. 2: group work is permitted where it is necessary to achieve the training goal, or where the young person has completed vocational training for that work - and in both cases only if their protection is assured through the supervision of a competent person. So (d) is too absolute and (c) exactly right. (a) overlooks that training necessity alone is not enough: competent supervision must be added.

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-28.question: During a peak in orders, an apprentice regularly works one hour beyond the agreed daily training time. How is that to be handled?

options.a: Extra work is covered by the training allowance, because that is paid as a lump sum
options.b: Employment beyond the agreed regular daily training time must be specially remunerated or compensated by corresponding time off
options.c: Extra work is prohibited for apprentices without exception
options.d: Extra work may only be performed with the competent chamber's consent

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-28.explanation: § 17(7) BBiG is unambiguous: "Employment beyond the agreed regular daily training time must be specially remunerated or compensated by the granting of corresponding time off." The company thus has a choice between payment and time off, but no option to leave the extra work unpaid - (a) is wrong, especially as the payment or compensation of overtime must expressly appear in the contract record under § 11(1) sentence 2 no. 8 BBiG. There is no absolute ban (c) in the BBiG; for young people, however, the limits follow from § 8 JArbSchG (at most eight hours a day, 40 hours a week) and from the proportionality requirement of § 14(3) BBiG - extra work that does not serve the training purpose is impermissible regardless of pay. Chamber consent (d) is not required. Professionally, regular extra work should be a warning sign: it suggests the apprentice is being deployed as labour rather than as a learner.

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-29.question: An apprentice arrives on time, but the training measure planned for him is cancelled because the machine has broken down. Later he is off sick for five weeks through no fault of his own. What applies to the allowance?

options.a: In both cases the allowance lapses, because no work is performed
options.b: The allowance lapses only for the illness; the machine breakdown is at the company's expense
options.c: In both cases the allowance must continue to be paid - on cancellation because he held himself ready, and for unavoidable prevention for a reason personal to him, in each case for up to six weeks
options.d: The allowance must be paid indefinitely, as long as the training relationship exists

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-29.explanation: § 19(1) BBiG governs three continuation grounds. No. 1: for periods of release under § 15 BBiG - here without a time limit. No. 2(a): for up to six weeks where apprentices hold themselves ready for training but it is cancelled - exactly the machine breakdown, which therefore falls to the company and does not affect the duty to pay. No. 2(b): for up to six weeks where they are prevented, through no fault of their own, for another reason personal to them - which covers the illness. Five weeks falls within those six. So (a) and (b) are wrong. (d) overlooks the six-week limit in no. 2; after that, statutory health-insurance sick pay normally takes over. § 19(2) BBiG adds that benefits in kind that cannot be taken during the continuation period must be compensated at the notional values. For training planning, one practical consequence: downtime costs the company anyway - a fallback plan for cancelled training measures makes economic sense too.

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-30.question: Which duties does § 13 BBiG place on apprentices? (4 correct answers)

options.a: To follow the instructions given to them in the context of their training by persons authorised to instruct
options.b: To keep trade and business secrets confidential
options.c: To obtain training means and technical literature at their own expense
options.d: To take part in training measures for which they are released under § 15 BBiG
options.e: To treat tools, machines and other equipment with care

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-30.explanation: § 13 BBiG first sets out a general clause: apprentices must endeavour to acquire the occupational competence required to reach the training goal. Sentence 2 then lists eight specific duties: no. 1 carry out assigned tasks carefully; no. 2 take part in training measures for which they are released under § 15 BBiG; no. 3 follow instructions given by training providers, trainers or other persons authorised to instruct, within the context of the training; no. 4 observe the establishment's rules; no. 5 treat tools, machines and other equipment with care; no. 6 keep trade and business secrets confidential; no. 7 keep a written or electronic training record; no. 8 confirm receipt of the contract record. Answer (c) is the exact opposite of the legal position: under § 14(1) no. 3 BBiG the training provider must supply the training means, including technical literature, FREE of charge. Note the limit in no. 3: the right to instruct exists only "within the context of the training" - instructions to perform work unrelated to training are caught by § 14(3) BBiG, not justified by it.

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-31.question: In your company, training is in practice organised "as orders allow"; there is no training plan, and whichever colleague happens to have time takes charge. Which breaches of duty are present?

options.a: None - the organisation of training is at the company's free discretion
options.b: Only a breach of the training regulation, not of the BBiG
options.c: Only a breach of the establishment's suitability under § 27 BBiG
options.d: Two breaches of § 14(1) BBiG: training must be delivered systematically, structured in time and substance, so that the training goal can be reached within the planned period (no. 1), and the provider must train personally or expressly commission a trainer to do so (no. 2)

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-31.explanation: § 14(1) no. 1 BBiG obliges training providers to ensure occupational competence is delivered, and to conduct the training "in the form required by its purpose, systematically, structured in time and substance, so that the training goal can be reached within the planned training period". Organising by order intake without a plan breaches that. § 14(1) no. 2 BBiG additionally requires "training personally or expressly commissioning a trainer to do so" - shifting de-facto responsibility without an express commission does not satisfy it; § 28(2) BBiG further requires the appointed trainer to deliver the content directly, responsibly and to a substantial extent. So (a) is wrong. (b) and (c) each name only a partial aspect: deviating from the training regulation does also breach § 4(3) BBiG, and the lack of planning indirectly touches the suitability question - but the provisions directly violated are the two duties in § 14(1) BBiG. § 3(2) no. 1 AEVO makes drawing up the company training plan a trainer competence for exactly this reason.

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-32.question: You notice that an apprentice is regularly put under pressure in the team through disparaging remarks and exclusion. What follows for you?

options.a: Nothing legal - the tone within a team is a social matter with no bearing on a trainer's duties
options.b: A statutory duty to act: training providers must ensure that apprentices are developed in their character and are not endangered morally or physically - alongside the AEVO competence of recognising problems and conflicts in good time and working towards a solution
options.c: You should wait to see whether the team sorts itself out and only step in on a formal complaint
options.d: You must move the apprentice to another department; no further measures are provided for

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-32.explanation: § 14(1) no. 5 BBiG contains an often-overlooked but real legal duty: training providers must ensure "that apprentices are developed in their character and are not endangered morally or physically". Systematic belittling and exclusion within a team falls under this, which is why (a) is wrong. Added to that is § 3(3) no. 7 AEVO: promote social and personal development, "recognise problems and conflicts in good time and work towards a solution" - "in good time" rules out the waiting in (c), and a formal complaint is not a precondition. The 2023 Rahmenplan expressly names, in HF 3.7, "measures to prevent psychological and physical strain" and the role-model function of trainers, and requires "reflecting on the causes of training dropout and taking measures to avoid it". (d) is an isolated measure that leaves the group's behaviour untouched: a transfer can be part of the solution but does not replace the conversation with the team, clear boundary-setting, and follow-up. Depending on the ground involved, the AGG and the employer's duty of care may also apply.

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-33.question: Your company is introducing a learning-management system with video modules and wants to use it to replace workplace instruction entirely. How do you assess that from a Handlungsfeld 3 perspective?

options.a: Sensible - digital media are more effective for learning than in-person instruction
options.b: To be rejected - digital learning media are not legally permitted in company training
options.c: It depends: the use of digital learning media and virtual or hybrid learning environments must be assessed, not adopted wholesale - media are selected to suit the method, and psychomotor objectives as well as learning-process guidance at the workplace cannot be replaced by video modules
options.d: Immaterial - the choice of media has no measurable effect on the learning outcome

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-33.explanation: The 2023 Rahmenplan expressly took digitalisation on board and requires in HF 3.4 "assessing the use of digital learning media and virtual and hybrid learning environments for training" - the verb is "assess", not "introduce", which is why (a) and (d) both miss the competence goal. The same section requires "describing the function of training media and aids and selecting and deploying them to suit the method" - so the choice of media follows the method, and the method follows the objective. For psychomotor objectives, practice at the real workplace remains indispensable, and the learning-process guidance the Rahmenplan highlights in HF 3.4 presupposes an accompanying person. (b) is legally wrong: § 28(2) sentence 2 BBiG expressly permits digital mobile training to an appropriate extent, provided information technology is used, the content and locations are suitable, and the quality of delivery is equivalent - and under § 14(1) no. 3 BBiG the hardware and software additionally required for it must be provided free of charge. A learning-management system is therefore a sensible building block, but no substitute for company-based training.

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-34.question: The 2023 Rahmenplan newly and expressly incorporated sustainability into the competence profile. How do you implement that in Handlungsfeld 3?

options.a: Through a one-off information session on the company's environmental management
options.b: By guiding apprentices towards sustainable action within the learning and working process, building sector- and company-specific sustainability aspects into the learning and work tasks, and reflecting on work assignments about changes in the world of work together with the apprentices
options.c: By leaving the topic to the vocational school, which has its own learning field for it
options.d: By assessing apprentices' personal environmental behaviour in every appraisal conversation

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-34.explanation: The 2023 Rahmenplan names sustainability in its foreword as one of three reasons for modernisation (alongside digitalisation and heterogeneity) and anchors it in several places. In HF 3.3 it expressly requires "guiding apprentices towards sustainable action within the learning and working process" and "preparing them for the scope to shape transformation processes", with the example content "sector- and company-specific aspects of sustainability" and "work assignments on changes in the world of work and reflection on them, e.g. changes in work organisation, the introduction of new technologies, sustainability". In addition, HF 2.1 requires "planning training with a view to promoting sustainability-related competences", and HF 1.1 names sustainability and future viability when justifying company-based training. The common thread is integration into the learning and work tasks - which is why (a), as a single event, falls short. (c) overlooks that the Rahmenplan assigns the competence to the trainer, not the school. (d) confuses occupational competence with private conduct: what is appraised under HF 3.8 is learning and working behaviour, against criteria, not private behaviour.

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-35.question: A 17-year-old apprentice reacts to criticism with growing irritation, tests boundaries and questions rules, but performs well technically. How do you classify this?

options.a: As a clear lack of aptitude justifying termination of the training relationship
options.b: As a discipline problem to be answered with a written warning
options.c: As possibly developmentally typical behaviour in adolescence - first factor in young people's developmental tasks and social influences, then respond with clear, reasoned rules, participation and delegated responsibility; genuinely conspicuous behaviour is distinguished from this and, where appropriate, addressed with specialist services
options.d: As purely a communication problem of the trainer's, needing no further consideration

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-35.explanation: § 3(3) no. 7 AEVO requires "promoting apprentices' social and personal development". The 2023 Rahmenplan spells out in HF 3.7: "describing young people's developmental tasks in training" and "taking developmentally typical behaviour and significant social influences into account when designing the training" - boundary-testing and the drive for autonomy in adolescence are therefore built into the competence profile as normal phenomena, not as a disorder. The Rahmenplan expressly distinguishes these from "conspicuous behaviour, e.g. anxiety, aggression, addictions", for which other routes apply - that is where specialist services come in. So (a) and (b) are premature: they sanction before the classification is clear, and (a) additionally overlooks that after probation a termination under § 22(2) no. 1 BBiG requires good cause. (d) shifts the cause entirely onto the trainer and blanks out the developmental perspective just as (a) and (b) do - the Rahmenplan does also require, in HF 3.7, "reflecting on one's own communication behaviour", but as one element among several, not as a substitute for classification.

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-36.question: A company has paid the same monthly training allowance unchanged since the first year of training; the apprentice is now in the third year. How do you assess this?

options.a: Permissible, as long as the allowance was appropriate in the first year
options.b: Not permissible: the allowance must be appropriate AND must rise at least annually as the training progresses
options.c: Permissible if the company is not bound by a collective agreement
options.d: Permissible if the apprentice consents in writing

aevo-ausbildung_durchfuehren-36.explanation: § 17(1) BBiG contains two separate requirements: sentence 1 demands an appropriate allowance, and sentence 2 provides that the allowance rises "as the training progresses, at least annually". An allowance left unchanged over three years breaches sentence 2, even if the starting amount was appropriate - which is why (a) is wrong. The absence of collective-agreement coverage (c) does not change that: § 17(2) BBiG additionally sets a graded monthly minimum allowance for companies not bound by a collective agreement, whose base amount is updated annually and published by the Federal Ministry of Education and Research in the Federal Law Gazette, with uplifts of 18, 35 and 40 percent for the second, third and fourth years - so the duty to increase is made even more concrete there. The apprentice's consent (d) does not help, because § 25 BBiG voids agreements deviating to their disadvantage. Practically relevant additions: § 17(4) BBiG as a rule rules out appropriateness where the allowance falls more than 20 percent below the applicable collectively agreed pay, and § 18(2) BBiG requires payment by the last working day of the current calendar month at the latest.

aevo-ausbildung_abschliessen-01.question: Which conditions must an apprentice satisfy under § 43(1) BBiG for admission to the final examination? (3 correct answers)

options.a: They have completed the training period, or their training period ends no later than two months after the examination date
options.b: They have taken part in prescribed interim examinations and submitted a training record, in writing or electronically, via the training provider
options.c: They achieved at least a "satisfactory" grade in the most recent vocational-school report
options.d: Their training relationship is entered in the register of training relationships - or is not entered for a reason for which neither they nor their legal representatives are responsible
options.e: They have paid the examination fee

aevo-ausbildung_abschliessen-01.explanation: § 43(1) BBiG names exactly three admission conditions, corresponding to answers (a), (b) and (d). No. 1 contains the two-month rule, which allows an apprentice to sit the regular examination date even if the training period ends shortly afterwards. No. 2 combines two elements: participation in prescribed interim examinations (participation, not a particular result!) and submission of the training record via the training provider. No. 3 requires registration but softens it with the fault clause: a registration missed by the company must not disadvantage the apprentice. School grades (c) are not an admission condition - under § 37(3) BBiG the vocational-school result can merely be shown on the examination certificate on application. An examination fee (e) does not arise for apprentices at all: § 37(4) BBiG expressly provides that the final examination is free of charge for apprentices. Admission is decided by the chamber under § 46(1) BBiG; if it considers the conditions unmet, the examination board decides. § 3(4) no. 2 AEVO makes registration and flagging delivery-relevant particulars a trainer task.

aevo-ausbildung_abschliessen-02.question: A colleague asks why no interim examination takes place in a particular training occupation. Which explanation is correct?

options.a: Interim examinations were abolished generally by the BBiG reform
options.b: Interim examinations only take place in industrial/technical occupations
options.c: The interim examination is dispensed with where the training regulation provides for a final examination conducted in two temporally separate parts - or where the training regulation provides for crediting another completed vocational training of at least two years and the parties have agreed that credit for at least that duration
options.d: The interim examination is dispensed with where the apprentice has shortened the training duration

aevo-ausbildung_abschliessen-02.explanation: § 48(1) BBiG first states the principle: during the training, an interim examination must be held in accordance with the training regulation to determine the level reached, with §§ 37 to 39 BBiG applying mutatis mutandis. So (a) and (b) are wrong. § 48(2) BBiG then names exactly two grounds for dispensing with it: no. 1 the training regulation provides for a split final examination in two temporally separate parts - in which case the first part takes over the stock-taking function - and no. 2 the training regulation provides for crediting another completed vocational training of at least two years AND the parties have agreed credit of at least that duration. A shortening under § 8(1) BBiG (d) is not among them - it shortens the duration but leaves the interim examination untouched. Under § 48(3) BBiG, retrainees must be admitted to the interim examination on application. Practically important: PARTICIPATION in prescribed interim examinations is an admission condition for the final examination under § 43(1) no. 2 BBiG - the result, by contrast, is not.

aevo-ausbildung_abschliessen-03.question: An apprentice has failed the final examination. She asks how often she can resit and what it will cost her. What do you answer?

options.a: Once; the resit is subject to a fee
options.b: Twice; the final examination is free of charge for apprentices - and with a split examination, note that the first part cannot be resat on its own
options.c: Without limit, as long as the training relationship exists
options.d: Twice, but only with the training company's consent

aevo-ausbildung_abschliessen-03.explanation: § 37(1) sentence 2 BBiG: "In the event of failure, the final examination may be resat twice." Sentence 3 adds, for the split examination, that the first part cannot be resat on its own - its result carries into the overall examination. § 37(4) BBiG states briefly: "The final examination is free of charge for apprentices." So (a) and (c) are wrong. Company consent (d) is not required; registration is in practice made through the company, and § 3(4) no. 2 AEVO makes it a trainer task. Two follow-up points belong in the same conversation: under § 21(3) BBiG the training relationship extends, at the apprentice's request, until the next possible resit, by at most one year - the request must come from her, it does not happen automatically. And under § 5(2) sentence 1 no. 2 BBiG a training regulation may provide that, on failing the examination in a three- or three-and-a-half-year occupation building on a two-year one, the two-year qualification is obtained where at least sufficient performance was achieved in the first part - this requires an application by the apprentice.

aevo-ausbildung_abschliessen-04.question: An apprentice passed the final examination; the examination board announced the result on 12 June. The training contract sets 31 July as the end of the training period. When does the training relationship end?

options.a: On 31 July - the contractually agreed date governs
options.b: On 30 June - at the end of the month in which the examination was passed
options.c: On 12 June - where the apprentice passes the final examination before the end of the training duration, the training relationship ends on announcement of the result by the examination board
options.d: Only when the examination certificate is handed over

aevo-ausbildung_abschliessen-04.explanation: § 21 BBiG governs three routes to termination. Paragraph 1 is the base case: the training relationship ends when the training duration expires. Paragraph 2 displaces that base case on early success: "Where apprentices pass the final examination before the end of the training duration, the training relationship ends on announcement of the result by the examination board." What governs is therefore the announcement, not the contractual date (a), not a month-end (b), and not the handing over of the certificate (d). This has immediate practical consequences: from that day the right to an allowance under § 17 BBiG lapses, and anyone wanting to keep the person on must agree something beforehand - because under § 24 BBiG an employment relationship of indefinite duration is deemed to have been established where an apprentice continues to be employed afterwards without an express agreement. Paragraph 3 governs the reverse case: on failure, the relationship extends at the apprentice's request until the next possible resit, by at most one year. The certificate under § 16 BBiG must be issued on termination - it is a consequence, not a precondition, of termination.

aevo-ausbildung_abschliessen-05.question: An apprentice passed the final examination on 12 June. From 13 June she continues to work in her department; nothing was agreed about follow-on employment. What is the legal consequence?

options.a: The training relationship continues until the contractually agreed end of training
options.b: An employment relationship of indefinite duration is deemed to have been established
options.c: A fixed-term employment relationship of six months arises
options.d: No legal relationship arises; the continued work is a favour

aevo-ausbildung_abschliessen-05.explanation: § 24 BBiG: "Where apprentices are employed following the training relationship without anything being expressly agreed about it, an employment relationship of indefinite duration is deemed to have been established." The provision attaches to the end of the training relationship, which here occurred on 12 June under § 21(2) BBiG on announcement of the examination result - so (a) is wrong. The consequence is indefinite, not fixed-term: a fixed term requires written form under § 14(4) TzBfG and must be agreed before it starts, which rules out (c). (d) overlooks that § 24 BBiG imposes the consequence by operation of law. In practice this means the decision must be taken BEFORE the examination result. The Rahmenplan expressly names, in HF 4.4, "shaping the transition into an employment relationship" - that is exactly the preparation meant here. If company and apprentice want a fixed term, a trial employment relationship or some other arrangement, it must be agreed in writing beforehand; if no continued employment is intended, that must be communicated clearly so that simply carrying on working does not create an open-ended contract.

aevo-ausbildung_abschliessen-06.question: On completion of the training, an apprentice asks you for a certificate and wants conduct and performance to be assessed in it. What applies?

options.a: A certificate is only issued on request; conduct and performance must always be included
options.b: A certificate must always be issued; details of conduct and performance must always be included
options.c: A certificate is only issued if the apprentice passed the final examination
options.d: A certificate must always be issued on termination of the training relationship and must state the nature, duration and goal of the training as well as the skills, knowledge and abilities acquired; details of conduct and performance are only included at the apprentice's request

aevo-ausbildung_abschliessen-06.explanation: § 16(1) sentence 1 BBiG obliges training providers to "issue apprentices with a written certificate on termination of the training relationship" - without any request and irrespective of the examination result, which is why (a) and (c) are wrong. Sentence 2 permits electronic form with the apprentice's consent; sentence 3 provides that the trainer should also sign where the provider did not deliver the training personally. § 16(2) BBiG then distinguishes two tiers: the mandatory content (the "simple" certificate) covers the nature, duration and goal of the training and the occupational skills, knowledge and abilities acquired; details of conduct and performance (the "qualified" certificate) are only included at the apprentice's request. So (b) is wrong - the assessment is request-dependent, so that nobody carries a rating in their certificate against their will. The Rahmenplan names exactly this distinction in HF 4.3 ("simple and qualified certificate"), the formal requirements, "permitted and non-permitted content", and the legal effects of certificates. The training certificate under § 16 BBiG must be distinguished from the examination certificate, which the chamber issues under § 37(2) BBiG.

aevo-ausbildung_abschliessen-07.question: An employee without formal training has worked for five years in the occupation in which he wants to sit the final examination; the training duration in that occupation is three years. Can he be admitted to the examination?

options.a: No - admission is excluded without a training relationship
options.b: Yes: admission to the final examination must also be granted to a person who proves they have worked in the occupation for at least one and a half times the prescribed training duration - here at least 4.5 years
options.c: Yes, but only after twice the prescribed training duration
options.d: Yes, if he additionally attends vocational school retrospectively

aevo-ausbildung_abschliessen-07.explanation: § 45(2) sentence 1 BBiG governs the so-called external candidate examination: "Admission to the final examination must also be granted to a person who proves that they have worked for at least one and a half times the period prescribed as the training duration in the occupation in which the examination is to be taken." With a three-year training duration that is 4.5 years, so five years suffices. That makes (a) and (c) wrong. Sentence 2 counts training periods in another relevant training occupation as periods of occupational activity. Sentence 3 contains an important opening: the minimum-period requirement may be waived in whole or in part where certificates or other evidence make it credible that the occupational competence justifying admission has been acquired; sentence 4 requires foreign qualifications and periods of work abroad to be taken into account. Retrospective vocational-school attendance (d) is not a condition. Parallel routes are § 45(3) BBiG (admission following the § 1(6) BBiG assessment procedure with certified full comparability) and § 45(4) BBiG for fixed-term and former soldiers.

aevo-ausbildung_abschliessen-08.question: An apprentice wants to apply abroad in Europe after the examination and asks about a foreign-language version of her examination certificate. What applies?

options.a: The apprentice must commission and pay for a translation herself
options.b: Foreign-language versions exist only for master-craftsman certificates
options.c: On the apprentice's application, an English and a French translation must be attached to the examination certificate; on application, the result of vocational-school performance assessments must also be shown on the certificate
options.d: The training company issues the translation, because it grants the certificate

aevo-ausbildung_abschliessen-08.explanation: § 37(3) sentence 1 BBiG: "On the apprentice's application, an English and a French translation must be attached to the certificate." The responsible body is the competent chamber, which issues the examination certificate under § 37(2) sentence 1 BBiG - not the company, which is why (d) is wrong, and not the apprentice herself, which is why (a) is wrong. The provision contains no restriction to master-craftsman examinations (b). § 37(3) sentences 2 to 4 BBiG additionally provide that, on application, the result of vocational-school performance assessments must be shown on the certificate; the evidence must accompany the application unless the school is itself obliged under state law to transmit it. The chamber's examination certificate must not be confused with the company's training certificate under § 16 BBiG - both are issued at the end of training, but by different bodies and with different content. The Rahmenplan requires in HF 4.3 "distinguishing different types of certificate" and highlighting their significance for the labour market; in HF 4.4 it names the Europass as a Europe-wide recognised supplementary document.

aevo-ausbildung_abschliessen-09.question: A technically strong apprentice regularly collapses in mock examinations and reports mental blocks. How do you support him in terms of Handlungsfeld 4?

options.a: You substantially increase the practice pressure so he gets used to stressful situations
options.b: You stop further mock examinations, so as not to reinforce the anxiety
options.c: You work on both sides: the specific features of the exam situation and time management within it, a personal learning plan for exam preparation, and techniques against fear of failure and mental blocks - drawing also on external help such as exam-preparation courses or peer study groups
options.d: You apply to the chamber to postpone the examination date by a year

aevo-ausbildung_abschliessen-09.explanation: § 3(4) no. 1 AEVO requires preparing apprentices for the final or journeyman examination "taking the examination dates into account, and leading the training to a successful conclusion". The 2023 Rahmenplan gets very concrete in HF 4.1 and names exactly the two strands in answer (c): on the one hand "offering help with exam preparation and with avoiding exam failure" and "conveying the particular features of an examination situation", and on the other, as example content, "overcoming exam anxiety, e.g. fear of failure, mental blocks, time management in an exam situation, personal learning planning for exam preparation" as well as "specific (including external) aids and techniques for exam preparation, e.g. peer study groups, exam-preparation courses, practising on analogue and digital exam tasks, mock examinations". (a) confuses habituation with overload and reinforces the block. (b) removes precisely the instrument the Rahmenplan expressly recommends - mock exams work when they are debriefed and combined with techniques. (d) is not an available route: there is no "one-year postponement" on the company's application; extension under § 8(2) BBiG requires an application by the apprentice and an exceptional case, and § 21(3) BBiG only applies after a failed examination.

aevo-ausbildung_abschliessen-10.question: Two weeks before the final examination it emerges that an apprentice needs more time and enlarged task sheets because of a visual impairment. What must be done?

options.a: Nothing - examination conditions are identical for all candidates and cannot be changed
options.b: Examination-relevant particulars must be communicated to the competent chamber and reasonable adjustments applied for; the apprentice must be released for the examination and for training measures outside the establishment, and on the working day immediately preceding the written final examination
options.c: The company decides on deviating examination conditions itself and informs the examination board on the day
options.d: The apprentice must move the examination to the next date

aevo-ausbildung_abschliessen-10.explanation: § 3(4) no. 2 AEVO states this task expressly: "ensuring that apprentices are registered for examinations with the competent chamber and drawing its attention to particulars relevant to delivery". The Rahmenplan spells out in HF 4.1/4.2 "communicating apprentices' examination-relevant particulars to the competent chamber" and expressly names "applying for reasonable adjustments" alongside registration deadlines, the registration form and training records. The addressee is the chamber, because the examination is administered under § 39(1) BBiG by the examination boards it establishes and is governed by its examination regulation under § 47 BBiG - so (c) is wrong, the company cannot set examination conditions itself, and notification on the day of the exam comes too late. (a) is incorrect: reasonable adjustments do not change the requirements, only the conditions under which they are demonstrated. (d) is unnecessary. On release from work, the Rahmenplan expressly names the BBiG, the JArbSchG and collective agreements as the bases in HF 4.2: § 15(1) sentence 2 no. 4 BBiG covers attending examinations and external training measures, no. 5 the working day immediately before the written final examination; the allowance continues to be paid under § 19(1) no. 1 BBiG.

aevo-ausbildung_abschliessen-11.question: At the end of her training an apprentice asks about advancement routes that do not require going to university. How do you advise her?

options.a: Without a degree there are no formally higher qualifications; she should catch up on a technical school-leaving certificate
options.b: She should only attend in-company adaptation training, because the BBiG has no concept of advancement training
options.c: Higher vocational training under the BBiG offers three advancement levels - Certified Vocational Specialist, Bachelor Professional and Master Professional - and funding routes such as Aufstiegs-BAföG, gifted-learner funding or scholarships are available
options.d: Advancement training is only accessible after five years of occupational activity

aevo-ausbildung_abschliessen-11.explanation: § 3(4) no. 4 AEVO makes it a trainer competence to "inform and advise apprentices about in-company development paths and occupational further-training options". The Rahmenplan spells out in HF 4.4 "higher vocational training on three advancement levels as an equivalent alternative to academic pathways, DQR levels" and names as funding "gifted-learner funding, Aufstiegs-BAföG, scholarships". The legal basis is § 53a BBiG, which names the three levels: first level Certified Vocational Specialist, second level Bachelor Professional, third level Master Professional. § 1(4) BBiG distinguishes adaptation training (maintaining and adapting occupational competence) from higher vocational further training (broadening competence and occupational advancement) - which is why (b) is wrong. (a) misses exactly the equivalence the German Qualifications Framework is meant to express. (d) invents a blanket waiting period; admission requirements follow from the relevant further-training regulation and differ by qualification.

aevo-ausbildung_abschliessen-12.question: Your HR department is drafting a qualified training certificate. One draft sentence reads: "He was always endeavouring to fulfil the tasks assigned to him, and left us at his own request after repeated cause for complaint had arisen." How do you assess this?

options.a: Unobjectionable - the wording is benevolent and contains no open criticism
options.b: Unobjectionable if the complaints are documented
options.c: Only the second clause is objectionable; "always endeavouring" is a neutral description
options.d: To be rejected: a certificate must be truthful and benevolent and must not contain coded negative statements; "always endeavouring" is a recognised negative formula, and the reference to complaints is an impermissible addition that burdens the person's future working life

aevo-ausbildung_abschliessen-12.explanation: § 3(4) no. 3 AEVO requires "participating in the preparation of a written certificate on the basis of performance assessments" - the trainer therefore shares responsibility for what the certificate says, and under § 16(1) sentence 3 BBiG should even co-sign it where the provider did not train personally. The Rahmenplan expressly names in HF 4.3 the "wording of certificates, e.g. permitted and non-permitted content", the formal requirements (form and completeness), and the "significance of certificates, e.g. legal consequences, significance for the labour market, individual opportunities". Certificates are governed by the principles of truthfulness and clarity: the content must be accurate and benevolently worded and must not unnecessarily impede the person's career progress. "Always endeavouring" is the best-known coded phrase for "did not meet the requirements" and is therefore a covert negative signal - which is why (c) is wrong. The addition about complaints is an extraneous, burdensome insertion that good documentation does not make permissible - (b) confuses provability with permissibility. (a) misses the coding entirely. The right approach: substantively accurate performance statements in plain language, grounded in the ongoing appraisals from HF 3.8 - and details of conduct and performance only where the apprentice requests them under § 16(2) sentence 2 BBiG.
